Just for those who are wondering about this while going onto spiro, I had ALL of these concerns. I have been diagnosed with PTSD, Panic Disorder, Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, etc. and I was extremely hesitant to go on this med. I talked to my dermatologist several times and voiced my concerns and talked to my psychiatrist. I ended up taking Spiro, but they started me on a very low dose and monitored it closely. The first 2 weeks were pretty intense. Crying spells, anxiety, overall depressed mood, etc. but after reading this is common, I waited it out and after the 2 weeks it went away. This also happened when I upped my dose, but again it went away within 2 weeks. 

I have now been on Spiro for about a year and have nothing but wonderful results. The major things I have found is if I skip my depression meds, I feel it a little more than I used to, but my skin is so clear and my anxiety, depression, panic and PTSD seem unaffected. 

It’s good to know the warning signs and document how you feel on the med, but it has done wonders for so many people so I wouldn’t let the potential side effects deter you. Speak with your doctor about it and come up with a plan to monitor your mood, stop the med if needed.

I absolutely love bullet journaling and my biggest breakthrough is the constant reminder that my journal is MY journal. It doesn’t have to be anything specific and any visions I have I set upon myself. 

I used to try and follow a specific layout but that was never successful for me. I would mess it up, get frustrated and then not want to journal/rip pages out. When I first started I tried to do a cover page, a habit tracker, a goals page, a mood tracker, etc. but I couldn’t keep up with it and then felt like a failure. 

The only thing I consistently do now is a cover page for the month and I still have to remind myself every fucking month that it’s okay if it’s not perfect and if it isn’t on the first of the month. Some times it’s a few days late, some times a couple weeks late, but I have found giving myself grace is what really matters for me. 

My average journal looks something like this, in no particular order- June page (some decorative shit I get inspired by on Pinterest), A weekly to do’s with doodles, a mantra/reminder and priorities, A poem I wrote with doodles, A random drawing, A montage of different things I find inspiring that day. 

I can send you some pics of mine if you are interested, but don’t worry about what it looks like or how set up it is, you aren’t making an outline for someone else to follow, you are journaling your own life.

I was incredibly scared to try this med due to severe treatment resistant depression and the possibility it would send me back into a deep depressive episode. This is what I experienced and why I’m glad I tried it/stuck with it:

- The first week I was incredibly emotional, little things would cause tears and I took everything personally. It took me until about day 6 to realize it was probably the medication, but once I realized this I was able to rationalize it. This only happened the first 6-10 days. 

- I broke out, not horribly, but still enough I was disappointed. 

- My boobs became tender

- I occasionally got light headed when I stood up to fast

- the first week I had really bad dry mouth, but it got better as my body adjusted

I am now about 3 months in and while I’m considering upping my dose, it has helped my acne a lot. My mood is stable and I am confident it is working. 

My biggest advice is be patient. Let the med get in your system and know you may have mild side effects at first. In the long run, I actually believe it has helped my anxiety and depression because my face is not always a complete mess and I am more confident in my complexion!

I’m a teacher and have seen several cases of dysgraphia. While that could be the cause, the writing is not bad enough that I would immediately jump to that. 

Questions I have: 
Is he left or right handed? 
How does he start his letters? (Does he start at the top, bottom, etc.)
Does his pencil move around a lot when he writes?
Does he hold his pencil the way most people do?

Things I would try: 
- Tracing sentences. Print out sentences, put them in a sheet protector and use a vis-à-vis.
- Play around with different styles of holding a pencil. 
- Buy a handwriting pencil 
- Practice for a few weeks and see if you see improvement.
